speaker: Chris Wright, U.S. Energy Secretary
quote: Nearly 9 million barrels per day leaving through Hormuz, as a seven-day average.
note: Also reported by Reuters commentary of 2026-08-24.

speaker: Chris Wright, U.S. Energy Secretary
quote: About 15 million barrels per day of total regional flow: roughly 9 through Hormuz plus 5-7 via bypass pipelines and export routes.
note: Not a Hormuz-only figure; includes bypass routes.

speaker: U.S. officials
quote: About 10 million barrels per day exiting via the strait itself.
note: Axios described this as roughly half of prewar Hormuz volume.

speaker: U.S. officials
quote: 15 to 20 tankers entering and exiting each night in the U.S.-protected corridor.
note: Inbound plus outbound combined; not equivalent to loaded outbound tankers.

speaker: U.S. administration
quote: A claimed 15 million barrels moved on one particular day.
note: Exceptional single-day volume claim, not an average rate.

speaker: Chris Wright, U.S. Energy Secretary
quote: An average of about 8 million barrels of oil per day had left Hormuz over the prior seven days.
note: Later reading of the same seven-day series as c1; different windows, not a correction.

speaker: Chris Wright, U.S. Energy Secretary
quote: More than 17 million barrels of oil transited the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, a record since the Iran war began in late February.
note: On Sept. 14, at an IAEA meeting, Wright said the seven-day rolling average "has been going up and will continue to go up" and indicated this Sept. 1 total was actually closer to 18 million barrels (per BOE Report/Reuters coverage); that later figure is not itself in quotation marks in available reporting, so it is not entered as its own row — see PR summary.

speaker: Chris Wright, U.S. Energy Secretary
quote: Were at the highest since the start of the conflict, just under 11 million barrels a day, seven-day average of oil and oil products going out of the Strait on ship on water.
note: Made in a Bloomberg TV interview; reported by TASS. "Just under" 11 million recorded as 11.0 per existing ledger convention for rounded approximations (cf. c1's "nearly 9").

speaker: Chris Wright, U.S. Energy Secretary
quote: Over the past seven days, an average of 10 million barrels per day of crude and oil products have moved through the Strait of Hormuz.
note: Reported by Bloomberg (Sept. 13), alongside Wright cautioning that "counting on a consensual agreement with Iran today is certainly not a good bet." Third dated reading of the declining weekly-average series after c8 (Sept. 10, ~11 mb/d); not a correction of c8, a later window of the same moving average.
